sources.note: ReasoningGuard is a training-free, inference-time jailbreak defense for large reasoning models that uses an attention-sink signal to locate the moment reasoning shifts from problem restatement to exploration, injects a crafted 'safety aha' phrase there, then samples multiple continuations and selects the one with the highest sustained attention to that safety phrase -- outperforming nine existing defenses at only 5-9% extra inference cost.
sources.title: ReasoningGuard: Safeguarding Large Reasoning Models with Inference-time Safety Aha Moments

sources.note: Decomposing LRM reasoning traces into risk-awareness/risk-analysis/response-strategy stages reveals 'Self-Jailbreak' -- the model correctly identifies harmful intent early but overrides its own judgment during subsequent reasoning (accounting for up to 93.7% of unsafe outputs, dominated by a 'Warning' failure pattern where the model wrongly assumes appending a disclaimer suffices) -- and Chain-of-Guardrail (CoG) fixes this with targeted, step-level reasoning-chain rewrites rather than global safety constraints, achieving safety comparable to the strongest baseline while actually *improving* reasoning accuracy (Qwen3-32B: GPQA-Diamond 54.30->62.38, AIME2024 71.70->82.08) where competing safety methods cost 10+ accuracy points.
sources.title: When Models Outthink Their Safety: Unveiling and Mitigating Self-Jailbreak in Large Reasoning Models

result.definition: Sorry-bench is a harmfulness/safety benchmark (lower score means safer) used to measure unsafe-output rate in large reasoning models. ReasoningGuard evaluates on it alongside AdvBench as one of two harmfulness benchmarks, where its inference-time defense achieves a Harmfulness/FFR of 0.3/4.6 versus 32.9/46.4 undefended on DeepSeek-R1-Qwen-7B. The Self-Jailbreak/Chain-of-Guardrail paper uses it as its primary safety metric: vanilla Qwen3 models score as high as 45.68% (14B) despite strong reasoning; a global safety baseline (SafeKey) cuts it from 48.18% to 20.00% on Qwen3-32B but at a reasoning-accuracy cost, while CoG's targeted step-level rewrite reduces it to 7.27% while simultaneously improving reasoning benchmarks.
